# Orchestration (area `orchestration`)

Planner and workers, task lifecycle, questions, pause/stop, schedules, reminders, loops and continuity between turns.

Active decisions here. Run `tools/kb/run kb show <file>` for the ones governing one file, their tests and open work; never reword an owner decision (supersede it).

- **ORCH-300** (owner): FERB has no notification rules: no planner field, side entry, RPC, CLI command or policy hook for them.
- **ORCH-301** (owner): Delegated conversations (converse steps) and answering FERB's questions in chat stay.
- **ORCH-302** (owner): One checker role judges an attempt's conditions and chooses what comes next (accept, fix the answer, retry with instructions, ask the owner, accept as unconfirmed, fail). There is no separate dispatcher.
- **ORCH-303** (owner): The planner gets the running summary for everything older plus the last 20 exchanges word for word (20 owner messages and FERB's replies to them), never history filling the model's window. Long task reports appear in their short form. The last 20 exchanges are never shortened, folded or dropped, however long they are.
- **ORCH-304** (owner): The summary holds the recent ~2 weeks plus what is still open (waiting tasks, open questions, promises); older settled material falls out of it, since memory facts and episodes hold what lasts. It folds about every 20-40 exchanges, in the background after the reply; the planner reads only the latest summary.
- **ORCH-305** (owner): There is no separate map step: a do step may carry an input list, independent steps run in parallel, and plan validation keeps the check that every input is covered exactly once.
- **ORCH-306** (owner): Standing sends stay: they are the only way to send to recipients FERB found itself (not in the owner's words, not already known), and the only way an unattended run can do so. Recipients in the owner's words or approved once never ask anyway.
- **ORCH-307** (owner): Attempts are counted per task or plan step: worker runs in one attempt loop, not model calls, tool calls or time; each loop round starts at 0. After 5 failed attempts FERB pauses and asks whether to keep going: Yes allows 5 more, No stops with what it found. An unattended run can't ask, so it stops at 5 and reports.
- **ORCH-308** (owner): Pause ends the current attempt and marks the task paused, not cancelled: no task-end clean-up, no final answer, loop state kept. Resume continues in place with the owner's discussion as the update, on the shared wait-for-the-owner mechanism. The planner pauses a running task when the owner's words question, doubt or rethink it (its reading, no keyword list); a plain correction still steers live. No pause button in the app.
- **ORCH-309** (owner): A task is done when every outcome condition is verified; an unproven side detail is removed from the answer or marked inline (fix the answer, no redo), so FERB never states unseen things as fact. How the work was done is judged from code facts, not by the model. Done-unconfirmed only when an outcome itself can't be verified. Every answer: the answer first, then at most one short "Couldn't confirm: ..." line; no "Why work stopped" on finished work, no restated goal.
- **ORCH-311** (owner): A planner turn may take 90 s, then it replies plainly instead of hanging. The 180 s silence guard stays for the other non-worker calls; workers keep no time limit.
- **ORCH-312** (owner): Pausing stops the task's running terminal commands and audio listening and keeps only its tabs and progress. FERB mentions a paused task once a day ("<task> is still paused. Resume?"). Pausing a scheduled run pauses that schedule's next runs.
- **ORCH-313** (owner): Folders, recipients and sites, profile/account, worker type and standing scope are fixed when a schedule or reminder is made, and stated then so the owner can correct them; unattended runs never re-guess them.
- **ORCH-314** (owner): Failed scheduled runs add no check-in across runs: each failed run already reports in chat.
- **ORCH-315** (owner): When the configured runtime reports a usage limit or a sign-in failure, FERB says so once and offers another signed-in runtime with one tap. It never switches by itself (billing).
- **ORCH-317** (owner): Reminders and schedules can fire when the owner is back at the Mac instead of polling; a scheduled run that did nothing posts nothing. Back at the Mac means the Mac coming back into use: lid opened or wake from sleep, screen unlocked, login or restart. Input idleness is not away: watching a film without touching anything is still being at the Mac. The paused-task mention uses the same signal.
- **ORCH-318** (owner): Only messages sent before FERB's first reply to the previous one restart the turn: FERB restarts once and reads them together (related: folded in; unrelated: both answered). Later messages wait their turn, and messages that queued are read together in the next turn. Once FERB has replied, a running task is unaffected. Code enforces at most one restart per turn, and the 90 s planner limit covers the turn including its restart.
- **ORCH-319** (owner): A part is one of the owner's asks, not a plan step. The planner declares parts in the owner's order, each answered directly or by one answer step; code validates them (one answer source each, answer steps distinct and not wait/ask, each success condition in exactly one part, no summing-up step). Tool-free parts answer in the first reply. Each other part posts once, when its answer step's check accepts, recorded durably, never twice, also across restarts. No final summarizing call: code adds only its fixed lines and "N of M done".
- **ORCH-320** (owner): When the request gives an end ("until Nov 3", "for 2 weeks"), the schedule stores it (quote-checked like every side entry), stops after it, and its card counts down to it. No end date in the words: it runs until stopped.
- **ORCH-321** (owner): A payment card shows the name the owner saved the card under in FERB (recorded with the payment when a saved card entry filled it), never any card digits.
- **ORCH-322** (agent): Every tree runs as a plan of worker steps with dependencies; a single task is a one-step plan. Step kinds are do (optional input list; an optional repeat rule makes it a loop), wait, ask and converse. A loop is a do step with a repeat rule on the same path, ending on a verified condition or a stop.
- **ORCH-323** (agent): Tree, step, loop round and conversation turn share one status function, one finish function, one stop check and one injected clock. "Needs the owner" means one thing everywhere: pause in place and ask; an unattended run declines at once. task.finished is published once per tree.
- **ORCH-324** (agent): A typed per-turn object carries a chat turn; one exit applies side entries, records the reply and lets the chat go. One quote check (memory.items.quoted) serves every side entry (remember, until, timers, schedules, changes, cancels, forget, conversation changes). One continue verb corrects running and ended tasks.
- **ORCH-325** (agent): Planner context goes: instructions, stable facts, running summary, recent conversation (append-only), then the live facts, time, front window, task state and open questions, then the new message (2026-11-03: no pushed memory or activity, ORCH-515; the lookup tools' schemas are fixed per install, so they don't move the cached prefix). Live values stay out of the cached prefix: {capabilities} names the paired owner profiles only, and whether each is connected now is in "Layer 2 - right now".
- **ORCH-326** (agent): Beyond the last 20 exchanges the conversation folds into the summary once that tail holds FOLD_CHUNK_TOKENS (20k) or the whole tail passes RECENT_CONVERSATION_TOKENS + FOLD_CHUNK_TOKENS (35k), in calls of at most 20k each. The summary is asked to stay within SUMMARY_TOKENS (2k) and is cut to it when shown; SUMMARY_DAYS (14) is its ~2 weeks. A report's short form is its first paragraph, 300 chars.
- **ORCH-327** (agent): Task and schedule folders must each name one specific folder: the disk root, the home folder itself, /Volumes and iCloud Drive's root are sent back to the planner for repair (argument validity).
- **ORCH-328** (agent): A question's kind comes from structure (the capability or approval kind, or the asker's tag); answers record state and the chosen option, never typed words. An answer in chat to a question with options counts only as one of them: the owner's words exactly, else the planner's reading exactly, else FERB asks which. The owner's words stay the recorded answer.
- **ORCH-329** (agent): Typed cards come only from rows FERB itself wrote: timer and schedule rows, memory items, a tool call's recorded kinds, target and page facts with the owner's Yes, the sites list, the artifacts, a schedule's run. No text is read to choose or fill a card. A card standing for one of code's lines names it, and the notch leaves that line out.
- **ORCH-330** (agent): New planner schema fields add no union or nullable types: unused fields are "" or 0, and flags are plain booleans.
- **ORCH-331** (agent): A one-step scheduled run (not a watch) that found nothing its request asks to tell and did nothing posts nothing (nothing_to_tell). The worker's word alone never silences a run: one whose tree has an acting call that ran without an error (cards.ACTING_KINDS) posts whatever its worker reported. Multi-step scheduled plans and planner replies always post.
- **ORCH-332** (agent): A chat.part record's seq is the UTC time to the microsecond as an ISO string, strictly increasing also across a restart.
- **ORCH-333** (owner): There is no separate resource reviewer: code records what the task closed or left open, and the merged checker judges it with everything else.
- **ORCH-334** (owner): A schedule's repeat interval is the owner's: code requires only a positive number, and no prompt sets a floor.
- **ORCH-500** (agent): intro.preview runs the real planner turn alone (Supervisor.preview): no run token, no worker, no task row, no chat entry; every event (plan, one part per planned step, done) carries preview: true. Its context leaves out the owner's live state (running tasks, open questions, earlier chat, notices, schedules, reminders) and keeps the capability facts; with no run token it has no lookups (ORCH-516), so no memory or activity. Its session prefix `preview:` is reserved, so chat.send refuses it. FERB.app only.
- **ORCH-501** (owner): The planner, workers and the orchestrator's recovery write no separate short version: a direct reply streams its full text, and a task's answer is the full answer with the side lines FERB adds. Question cards keep their own display text.
- **ORCH-503** (owner): For a big job the plan line states the plan, estimates and any standing scope, and work starts at once; the owner corrects by replying. Escape-hatch commands and retries after an unknown outcome still wait; steering never records a No; a retry the owner drives re-asks a No once.
- **ORCH-504** (owner): The daemon sends an instant acknowledgement from the owner's approved phrase list (ferb/orchestrator/acks.py, without the starred phrase), never one of the last eight used.
- **ORCH-505** (owner): A loop with no stated end runs until the owner says stop, across restarts and updates; when fixes don't last it backs off and tells the owner once; constants: backup round 1,800 s; didn't last within 120 s; 3 such in 600 s start back-off at 120 s doubling to 3,600 s; reset after 1,800 s; look-only rounds skip the check; held tabs return between rounds.
- **ORCH-506** (owner): Long-running watches run without AI calls (reload, read and view-switch clicks set up once), with a 30 s floor; FERB looks up the service's rate limits and says which interval it chose.
- **ORCH-507** (owner): A question stays open as long as its task waits, with no expiry. Codex's FERB tool timeout is MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT_S (7 days) and Claude Code's MCP tool idle timeout is off (CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_TOOL_IDLE_TIMEOUT=0), so a waiting tool call isn't cut by the runtime.
- **ORCH-508** (agent): A stop from another chat stops a running task; a stop that arrives after the work finished leaves that work done, never cancelled; an answer to a question no longer waiting keeps the planner's own reply.
- **ORCH-509** (agent): An attempt whose report fails validation reports nothing of an earlier attempt, and a correction delivered while the check runs keeps the finished report for the next attempt, which starts from the correction.
- **ORCH-510** (agent): A clean shutdown runs no task-end clean-up for a task tree that resumes at the next start, so the change records startup keeps for it survive.
- **ORCH-511** (agent): An every-schedule resumed before its first run keeps that first run; a schedule whose timer was handled but not rebooked is rebooked once at start; a scheduled run never overlaps its previous run.
- **ORCH-512** (agent): A scheduled run keeps the recipients the owner said (a remembered address never rewrites them), and what an earlier run read from outside keeps its outside origin when the next run is shown that answer.
- **ORCH-513** (agent): A correction records only destinations the owner named, keeps pasted text and attachments as untrusted data, never widens a task's identity or scopes, redacts secrets before the worker and storage, and never answers a question or approves a payment, secret or plan unless the owner's own words name it.
- **ORCH-515** (owner): Every planner turn gets its instructions with Tier 1, the summary and last 20 exchanges (ORCH-303), tasks running or waiting on the owner, open questions and live facts. Memory, older or other chats, this chat's other ended tasks and today's activity are not pushed: the planner looks them up, read-only, through FERB's gateway (ORCH-516). Kept from ORCH-1: the planner changes nothing until it returns; an observation or action on the Mac is a task. Kept from MEM-16: messages and FERB's short replies are in the fused search; chat.history searches by meaning and date, paging from the database.
- **ORCH-516** (agent): A planner call (not the intro preview: no run token) gets a run token for only PLANNER_TOOLS (memory.read, chat.history, task.evidence, trail.query, trail.days), observe-only, at most PLANNER_LOOKUPS (10) calls, for a live lookup record with no task row lent the turn's chat; all end with the call. Results reach the model as worker results do (redacted, with their origin line); their origins join the turn's and each becomes a planner read on its task, which the sink rule counts. No skill or ability catalog; a tool call restarts the reply draft.
- **ORCH-517** (agent): task.evidence takes an optional task_id: a task of the caller's conversation (the conversation of the caller's registered record, never a name), read whole (its tree's tool calls, records and reports) with that task's own origins; any other id is refused. Without it the tool reads the caller's own task as before.
